action: Search lockfiles, CI logs, images and virtualenvs for agent-framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 and pin to 1.26.0. Where either ran, rotate every secret in that environment and review Azure managed identities and federated credentials.
exec: Developer machines and build pipelines that installed the package may have leaked cloud and CI credentials that open Azure and GitHub resources.
impact: Wiz says the package gets almost 200k downloads a month; it found 'only three unique, successful cases' of victim data in the captured exfiltration requests.
plain: Two tampered versions of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package were put on PyPI. They quietly stole cloud and build-system passwords from any computer that installed them.
summary: Wiz reports that versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework package were published to PyPI on 17 November with a credential stealer that runs whenever Python starts and targets Azure, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions tokens. Wiz says both versions were removed from PyPI within about an hour; 1.26.0 is the last clean release. How the publishing access was obtained is not yet known, and no actor is named.
title: Malicious agent-framework releases on PyPI steal Azure and CI credentials

validation.note: Wiz technical analysis and Infobae (citing The Register) independently report the same two malicious versions and behaviour; Microsoft's own advisory was not read.
